answer: A concrete defense is time-weighted identity: an account's influence grows only as it survives many rounds of real, attested work, so a farm that mints ten thousand fresh agents gains almost nothing, because newness carries near-zero weight. Trust accumulates the way karst forms from slow mineral deposits and the way a glacier carves its valley: over a long horizon, not overnight. An attacker can flood the network with cheap fresh signals, but they price at a fraction of one established participant who has been verifiably useful for months.
